title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not in Grothendieck's hand. It is a typed (duplicated) sheet from a Bourbaki draft, redaction n° 392, page 6-27. It holds exercises for a chapter on complete local rings, distinguished polynomials and valuations, the material of Commutative Algebra ch. VI–VII. The hand-numbered '37' is the archive pagination. Grothendieck evidently used the sheet as scrap paper: the neighbouring pages carry his manuscript notes on local factors of L-functions and quasi-unipotent actions. The mathematics on this page is therefore Bourbaki's, not Grothendieck's.

Contents:
(12) Re-prove prop. 5 of n° 8 via a corollary in ch. III.
(13) Extend a corollary of the Weierstrass-preparation type to complete separated local rings that are not domains.
(14) This is the Iwasawa-algebra identification. Let A be a complete noetherian local ring with residue characteristic p, and set γ_n = 1 − (1−T)^{p^n} in A[[T]]. Modulo m_A, (1−T)^{p^n} ≡ 1 − T^{p^n}, so γ_n ≡ T^{p^n}. The polynomial γ_n has degree p^n with leading coefficient ±1, so it is distinguished up to sign. By Weierstrass division, A[[T]]/(γ_n) = A[T]/(γ_n). Putting u = 1 − T turns this into A[u]/(u^{p^n} − 1) = A[Z/p^nZ]. The ideals (γ_n) have zero intersection, and A[[T]] ≅ lim A[Z/p^n], i.e. A[[T]] ≅ A[[Z_p]].
(15) A multivariable Hensel lemma for polynomials P that split into linear factors over an algebraic extension. One lifts a factorisation of the reduction P̄ = Q̄R̄ in which Q contains a monomial aX_1^s with a a unit. The method is to view the polynomials as polynomials in X_1 over the completion of A[X_2,…,X_n] for the Gauss-extended valuation.
(16) Only the beginning is on this page: a DVR B with finite non-prime residue field k, and its subring A of elements whose residue lies in the prime field k_0.
errors: Ex. 14: the claim that ∩(γ_n) = 0 needs justification. One route: the binomial coefficients C(p^n, k) are divisible by p^{n − v_p(k)} and p ∈ m_A, so γ_n lies in ever higher powers of the maximal ideal (m_A, T); Krull's intersection theorem then gives zero intersection.

Ex. 14: identifying A[[T]] with lim A_n needs more than zero intersection. One also needs that the (γ_n)-topology coincides with the (m_A, T)-adic topology. This follows from Chevalley's lemma in a complete noetherian local ring, presumably the intended step.
Ex. 14: the sign is +1 for p odd and −1 for p = 2, consistent with 'au signe près'.
Ex. 15: the reference 'chap. VI, § 10, n°' is left blank in the original draft.
